claims.text: A controlled nanocrystalline oxide scale is the governing factor that improves the high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating on a conventional steel substrate without a deliberately pre-formed oxide scale.
Annealing at 600 °C for 1 hour under regulated oxygen will form a coherent nanocrystalline oxide scale on FeNiCrCoCu.
The protective scale will be continuous and contain Cr2O3 and mixed-metal oxides.
The oxide scale will adhere well to the underlying FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The pre-formed oxide scale will passivate the coating and limit further oxidation during high-temperature wear.
The oxide scale will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact and thereby reduce adhesive wear.
A nanocrystalline oxide structure can accommodate cyclic strain without cracking.
The oxide scale will reduce abrasive wear and spallation in addition to adhesive wear.
The pre-annealed coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the as-deposited coating.
The pre-annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
After wear testing, the nanocrystalline oxide scale will remain largely continuous and well adhered.
The proposed oxide-mediated protection applies over a wear-test temperature range of 500–700 °C.
The proposed mechanism remains effective under moderate-to-high cyclic contact stresses.
Loads or prolonged exposure that cause oxide-scale spallation will eliminate the protective mechanism.
Excessive oxide thickening or degradation will cause the protective mechanism to break down.
The long-term stability and adhesion of the oxide scale under prolonged cyclic loading are uncertain.
The optimal annealing conditions for consistently producing a non-spalling protective scale are not established.
